title: How OpenAI bet on one idea: Sam Altman on conviction, scale, and building in an AI platform shift
summary: Sam Altman recounts how OpenAI won against better-resourced labs by concentrating on one bet (deep learning that improves with scale) and holding conviction until data said otherwise. He also covers peer groups, speed as a startup's edge in platform shifts, and why AI demos are not businesses.

principles.text: Concentrate on one bet when under-resourced; competitors spread across many things, so pick one and push hard.
principles.quote: we were far less resourced than Deep Mind and others and so we said okay they're going to try a lot of things and we've just got to pick one and really concentrate and that's how we can we can win here

principles.text: Extreme conviction on a single bet is underappreciated by most of the world.
principles.quote: most of the world still does not understand the value of like a fairly extreme level of conviction on one bet

principles.text: Conviction must be paired with truth-seeking: run on conviction without data, then follow the results the moment data arrives.
principles.quote: conviction is great until the moment you have data one way or the other and there are a lot of people who hold on it past the moment of data

principles.text: If something improves with scale, scale it; more is often more.
principles.quote: if you have something that seems like it's getting better with scale I think you should scale it up

principles.text: A startup's number one edge is speed, focus and conviction; build the same day you see a new technology, not in a quarterly plan.
principles.quote: your advantage with speed and focus and conviction and the ability to react to to how fast the technology is moving that is that is the number one edge of a startup kind of ever

principles.text: A new technology doesn't suspend business rules; demos are easy, but you still have to build a durable business.
principles.quote: everyone can build an incredible demo but building a business man that's the brass ring the rules still apply
